articleTitle: Trump Launches Super Intelligence Force to Coordinate U.S. AI Policy

sources.title: Trump unveils his new Super Intelligence Force - TechCrunch
After White House accord, Trump announces formation of Super Intelligence Force to ‘ensure US lead in AI’ | Hindustan Times
Bigger than industrial revolution: Trump announces Super Intelligence Force
Trump forms 'Super Intelligence Force' to cement US dominance in next-gen AI

claims.claim: In a recent executive order, former President Donald Trump announced the creation of the Super Intelligence Force (SIF).
claims.bestSource: Trump unveils his new Super Intelligence Force - TechCrunch
claims.evidence: Trump outlined the wide scope of outreach to "ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence.""The Super Intelligence Force is tasked with coordinating the effort of the Federal Government to ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence, which many say is bigger than the Industrial Revolution, and the Internet, and will protect the interests, and improve the lives, of all Americans," he wrote.Trump specified that the Super Intelligence Force will coordinate government engagement with "Federal Government's engagement with Consumers, Public Interest Groups, Religious Organizations, Critical Infrastructure Providers, and Super Intelligence Companies."The Super Intelligence Force will be led by a four-member leadership team spanning national intelligence, defence, regulatory, and federal personnel operations. Venture capitalist David Sacks and former Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice will serve as external advisers.Sacks held the AI czar role at the start of Trump’s second term.TRUMP’S PUSH FOR ‘SUPER INTELLIGENCE’Trump described superintelligence as a technology that “many say is bigger than the Industrial Revolution, and the Internet”.He had announced the terminology change at the UN General Assembly, arguing that the word “artificial” made the technology sound fake.“The use of the word artificial intelligence makes it sound fake, and it is not fake. Since then, Trump signed an executive order seeking to rebrand AI as “super intelligence,” a term seemingly embraced, with some stumbles , by the tech executives who gathered at the White House this week to sign a non-binding safety pledge. (The pledge included an impressive typo .)

editorial.claim: The inclusion of high‑profile technologists and former policymakers signals an intent to blend industry expertise with federal coordination.
However, the non‑binding safety pledge signed by tech leaders—though it contained a typo—suggests that regulatory authority remains limited.
Readers should monitor how the SIF’s activities evolve, particularly its interactions with private firms and its approach to balancing innovation with public protection.
